subject: math

objective.text: Solve word problems that compare two amounts. Find how many more or how many fewer.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective (Solve compare with difference unknown problem types)

explanations.title: Find the missing part
explanations.text: Rose wrote 8 letters. Her goal is 12 letters. Draw a tape for the 8. The total is 12. The missing part is how many more she needs. Think 8 plus what number makes 12. Or take 8 away from 12.

explanations.title: Compare with two tapes
explanations.text: Draw one tape for each amount. Put them one above the other. The longer tape is the bigger number. The extra piece on the longer tape shows how many more.

explanations.title: Subtract to compare
explanations.text: Nikil wrote 12 letters. Rose wrote 8 letters. Cover up the 8 on Nikil's tape. What is left is how many more. That is 12 minus 8. We can use subtraction to compare.

explanations.title: More and fewer go together
explanations.text: If Nikil wrote 4 more letters, then Rose wrote 4 fewer letters. It is the same difference. We find it with the same subtraction.

assets_required.why_this_method: Tape diagrams need exact relative lengths and labeled numbers. Diffusion cannot keep tape lengths to scale.
assets_required.description: A tape diagram on a plain background. One mode shows a single tape with parts 8 and a question mark under a total arm of 12. The other mode shows a double tape diagram: two tapes one above the other, labeled R (8) and N (12). Nikil's tape has a dotted split after 8 and the extra piece is circled with a question mark.
must_show_exactly: Single tape mode: a tape labeled R with 8, a second part with a question mark labeled M, and a total arm of 12
Double tape mode: exactly 2 tapes, one above the other, left ends lined up
Tape R holds 8 and tape N holds 12; tape N is longer, to scale
Tape N is split by a dotted line after 8; the extra piece is circled and holds a question mark
Numbers can be swapped to other values (9 and 11, 13 and 8, and so on) with the tape lengths still to scale
states_or_frames: State 1: single tape with the missing part
State 2: double tape with both tapes drawn
State 3: double tape with the dotted split and circled extra piece
assets_required.interaction: Child can reveal the dotted split. No typed input inside the widget. The text of the question comes from the chat.
assets_required.alt_text: Two tapes one above the other. The lower tape is longer. The extra piece is circled with a question mark.
assets_required.review_notes: The source refers to pictures with 'as shown to the right' but the .md file has no pictures. Build the layout from the words only; compare it with the original lesson.
assets_required.generation_caption: Clean double tape diagram: two rectangles one above the other, left ends lined up, the lower one longer, a dotted split and a circled extra piece, labels R and N, plain background. [Build by code]

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.

Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
